To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Penning ionization spectra of acene molecules embedded in He nanoclusters are broad and structureless.

Penning spectra measured in the gas phase and in He nanodrops are very different, that the spectra measured in He nanodrop experiments are not reproduced by simulations that do not include electron-He interactions and that these spectra are not reproduced by the simulations when assuming the droplet size to be the same as in the gas phase.
Penning electron spectra of embedded molecules are broadened and featureless due to collective electron-helion interactions, which can be reproduced by simulations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the Penning ionization of molecules in helium nanodrops by synchrotron photoionization and electron scattering.
the study of the electronic structure of organic molecules in helium nanodrops.
the study of molecular systems embedded in helium nanoclusters and their interaction with EUV radiation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Penning spectra of embedded molecules are not only affected by the droplet size but also by collective electron-droplet interactions.
Penning spectra of embedded molecules in HeN are not only broadened but also strongly distorted by the collective electron-helion interactions in the droplet.

the measured Penning spectra of molecules embedded within helium nanodroplet clusters are dominated by electron scattering within the droplet, which is a collective effect, rather than by the Penning electron energy loss in the binary collisions of the Penning ionization process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the electron spectra measured by Penning ionization of molecules embedded in He nanosolvated systems (He droplet, He nanocluster, He matrix) are very sensitive to the local helium environment of the molecule.

Penning ionization of molecules embedded in He droplets is a complex process, and that the resulting spectra are not directly related to the molecular electronic states. This is in contrast to Penning ionization in gas-phase collisions,
the Penning ionization of molecules embedded in He nanoclusters is a complex process, which requires a careful theoretical treatment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Penning electron spectrum does not reflect the ionization potential of the molecule, but is rather dominated by the collective electron-helion interactions.
the interpretation of Penning electron spectra of molecules in He nanodrops is not as straightforward as previously assumed.
the Penning electron spectrum is not an unambiguous fingerprint of the ionized molecule, but rather of the entire system, including the embedding helium nanodroplet.
